chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ismail ibn Jabir who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying:
'The water of Zamzam is a healing from every illness' — and I think he said: 'Whatever it may be.'

key_terms.دَاءٍ: Da' — illness, disease, ailment; used in the broadest sense encompassing all maladies
key_terms.شِفَاءٌ: Shifa' — healing, cure, remedy; used in both physical and spiritual senses in Islamic literature
key_terms.كَائِناً مَا كَانَ: Ka'inan ma kan — 'whatever it may be'; an emphatic universal qualifier meaning without exception or limitation
key_terms.مَاءُ زَمْزَمَ: Water of Zamzam — the sacred well within the Masjid al-Haram in Mecca, believed to have sprung miraculously for Hajar (Hagar), the mother of Prophet Ismail (AS)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the healing properties of Zamzam water?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) declares that the water of Zamzam well in Mecca is a cure for every type of illness, without exception. The narrator Ismail ibn Jabir adds a qualification noting that he heard an additional phrase — 'whatever it may be' — though he is not entirely certain about this addition. This hadith reflects the sacred status of Zamzam water, which has been venerated in the Islamic tradition as a blessed and healing water since the time of Ibrahim (AS), and pilgrims to Mecca have always sought it for both physical and spiritual healing.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Ismail Bin Jabir who said,

en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Tsma‘il ibn Jabir who has said the following: “I once heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘
The water of Zamzam is a cure for all illnesses,’ I think he said, ‘no matter whatever it may be.’”
